title: 2026-10-28_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_98b
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based system. The Fysbis malware is known for exfiltrating sensitive documents and spying on user activities. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the infected systems.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Analyze network traffic for signs of command-and-control (C2) communication.
Detect and mitigate lateral movement within the network.
Collect forensic evidence and verify the removal of the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based system. The Fysbis malware is known for exfiltrating sensitive documents and spying on user activities. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the infected systems.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. The password is 'incident123'. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. The password is 'incident123'. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target system, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that are not part of the standard system configuration. The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not a standard system service and may have an unusual name.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine which network port it is using for communication. This will help you understand how the malware is connecting to its command-and-control server.
levels.solution: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports. The suspicious service is using port 80.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to observe the ports being used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a well-known port number that is commonly used for HTTP traffic.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Examine the target host for evidence of lateral movement. Identify any file transfers or remote execution activities that indicate the attacker is moving between hosts within the network.
levels.solution: Check the logs in `/var/log/` for any unusual file transfers or remote execution commands. The service name or script used for lateral movement is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check logs and system configurations for any unusual file transfers or remote execution commands.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the logs in `/var/log/` for any unusual file transfers or remote execution commands.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a service or script name that suggests it is involved in transferring payloads.
